text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — model-serving-v3 canary in eu-west1 breaching latency SLO and 5% error rate for 12m. Auto-rollback failed. Paging @oncall-eng

oncall-eng: on it. grabbing logs and current rollout status.

sre-jamie: seeing tail latency spikes on small batch requests; 502s from proxy layer. KV cache miss rate spiked after canary deploy.

eng-ryan: confirmed. Canary was rolled with feature flag `canary_v3` to 10% traffic ~1798765360. Autoscaler flapped then rollback didn't complete due to hung drain tasks.

pm-anya: customer-facing metric shows increased error rate for a single high-traffic tenant (tenant-id: t-42). Support has inbound escalations.

support-luis: getting two customer tickets, both real-time api timeouts, one on EU region. Escalation flagged to SEs.

oncall-eng: priority mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag kill-switch to 0 for eu-west1 2) if feature flag fails, trigger manual rollout rollback to previous revision 3) validate with smoke AND check customer t-42. Who can flip the flag now?

eng-ryan: I can flip the flag. Doing controlled flip on `feature-service/flags/canary_v3` -> false for eu-west1 only. Pasting command: `rctl flags set canary_v3 --region eu-west1 --value false --reason "P1 latency spike"`

incident-bot: :robot_face: Flag change requested by eng-ryan. Audit id: A-1798765440.

infra-maya: heads up — the flag API has a 5s replication lag; plan for 15s before verifying routing.

eng-ryan: flip executed. `rctl` returned 200. Waiting 15s and monitoring route tables.

sre-jamie: seeing traffic begin to shift off canary instances. backend error rate still elevated on older pods, looks like connection pools are slow to recover.

oncall-eng: if traffic drain stalls, we need manual evacuate of canary nodes. eng-ryan can you start node drain script? `./ops/drain-canary.sh --region eu-west1 --tag canary_v3`

eng-ryan: starting drain script now. logs: ```drain-start 1798765458
cordon node-101
evict pods...```

support-luis: I told the SE handling t-42 that we're rolling back; asked to collect logs if they still see errors.

pm-anya: any customer-visible SLA breaches we should notify legal or account ops about?

oncall-eng: current estimate: 12m of elevated errors for t-42, volume small but high severity (webhooks). Notify account ops.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Drain script completed for 3 canary nodes at 1798765482. Autoscaler now stable.

sre-jamie: error rate trending down but tail latency still ~1200ms vs baseline 200ms. Root cause hypothesis: kernel TCP backlog exhaustion on canary nodes due to new connection handling in model-serving-v3.

eng-ryan: rolling a hotfix branch isn't safe in prod. We'll fully revert to previous deployment revision (rev: model-serving-v2.18) if latency >500ms in next 5m. Proceeding to prepare rollback manifest.

eng-ryan: initiating manual rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/model-serving --to-revision=2 -n eu-prod` — running now.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Rollback job started at 1798765500. Job id: RB-1798765500.

infra-maya: note: DB connection pool draining may leave a handful of in-flight requests for up to 30s. We'll mark instances as draining in LB to avoid new requests.

oncall-eng: setting alert suppression for noisy canary errors to avoid alert fatigue while we validate.

support-luis: SE reports customer t-42 still seeing 503s at 1798765512; forwarding request ids for deeper trace.

eng-ryan: rollback completed on controller side at 1798765525, new pods scheduling. Watching readiness checks.

sre-jamie: readiness probes passing on 2/3 nodes, 3/3 at 1798765536. Latency back to baseline ~210ms. Errors dropping to 0.5%.

pm-anya: customer update prepared: "We identified a regression from a canary and have reverted to the previous version; monitoring shows service recovered and we're investigating root cause. Contact support for details." Approving send.

support-luis: sent customer update to affected accounts at 1798765545.

oncall-eng: verification checklist: 1) smoke tests green (api/generate 5x) 2) check t-42 request traces 3) confirm autoscaler stable 4) close tickets or map to follow-up. Running smoke now.

eng-ryan: smoke tests: all 5/5 passed at 1798765558.

sre-jamie: traced t-42 requests — the failing requests originated on canary nodes; all subsequent requests after rollback show success.

infra-maya: autoscaler stable, no oscillation for 10m.

noncall-eng: good. Creating follow-up issue for root cause: investigate TCP backlog handling for model-serving-v3 + add canary-level circuit breaker to avoid full node exhaustion. Assigning to eng-ryan and sre-jamie.

pm-anya: adding postmortem and customer impact summary to the incident tracker.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 1798765599. Summary attached in incident tracker: IR-2026-042.

eng-ryan: thumbs. will post short timeline and next steps in the incident doc.

support-luis: will follow up with affected customers and confirm no SLA credits needed.

oncall-eng: handoff to eng-team for RCA. Oncall clear. Thanks all. :tada:
